chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Salamah ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿĪsā Shalqān, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) had maternal kin among Banī Makhzūm, and a young man from them came to him and said, “O my maternal uncle, my brother has died, and I have grieved over him with intense grief.” He said to him, “Would you like to see him?” He said, “Yes.” He said, “Then show me his grave.”

He said: So he went out, and with him was the cloak of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), wrapped around him. When he came to the grave, his lips moved, then he struck it with his foot, and the man came out from his grave speaking in the Persian tongue. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said, “Did you not die while you were a man from the Arabs?” He said, “Yes, but we died upon the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of so-and-so and so-and-so, so our tongues were changed.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام), central figure in the narration.
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: The grave from which the deceased is brought forth.
key_terms.بُرْدَةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The cloak of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), carried as part of the event.
key_terms.حُزْنًا شَدِيدًا: Intense grief over the death of a loved one.
key_terms.سُنَّةِ فُلَانٍ وَفُلَانٍ: The way or tradition of unnamed individuals, contrasted here with the right path.
key_terms.فَانْقَلَبَتْ أَلْسِنَتُنَا: Our tongues were changed; indicating an altered posthumous state.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the state of a person after death and the authority of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an extraordinary event in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) shows a grieving relative his deceased brother. The report connects a person’s state after death with the path he followed in life, and presents this as a sign of the authority and miraculous capacity of the Imam. It also touches on barzakh and the consequences of religious allegiance after death.
